_comment: Every vehicle below is named explicitly in the handbook (Annex 14, Tables 11 & 13, and body text). Object-number-only designations (e.g. '429', '137') are kept exactly as the handbook writes them — no common name has been guessed, since misidentifying a hull is worse than leaving it blank. Dimensional specs (length/width/height/weight/COG/tie-down count) are NOT given anywhere in this handbook extract for any vehicle, so every vehicle carries explicit TODOs for those fields rather than an invented number. Three wheeled vehicles (ZIL-131, KamAZ-43114, Ural-4320) are NOT from the handbook: they come from the project's own design mockup (Berl/harby_yukleme_simulyator.html, const VEHICLES) and carry "dataSource": "designMockup" so nothing can present them as extracted handbook data. Without them the wheeled half of the source — plates 05 and 06, the wheeled chock count, the lateral chock gap, the three-axle doubling, KGUUB-1K/2K and the wire-lashing angle table — is unreachable in the app, because the catalogue held only tracked vehicles. The mockup states an UNLADEN weight ('boş'), which is not the combat weight the handbook's chock rules are keyed on. Each vehicle carries one weight — its own — in weightT, and says which kind it is in weightBasis; those three are marked 'unladen', so the weight is shown but withheld from every weight-keyed table rather than being used as the wrong quantity.

vehicles.class: Main battle tank (esasy söweş tanky) — T-72 "Ural", the service name of Object 172M; the handbook covers it as Object 172
vehicles.manufacturer: Uralvagonzavod
vehicles.country: USSR
vehicles.notes: THE HANDBOOK DOES COVER THIS VEHICLE, under its factory designation. Annex 14's Table 13 lists 'Object 172' inside the grouped entry veh-obj-family-137 (Objects 137, 155, 166, 172, 608 and the engineer vehicles beside them) and assigns that whole group iron spur type Ş-137. Object 172M is the T-72, so its securing method is not a choice: para. 31 mandates the iron spur, and the spur type comes from the handbook by name. That identification is the one thing here that is NOT from the handbook — the extract never writes the name 'T-72' — and it is why this record exists separately instead of the family entry being renamed, which the project's own rule forbids. The dimensions are the manufacturer's published specification for the baseline T-72: hull 6.86 m (9.53 m over the gun trained forward), 3.59 m wide, 2.19 m to the turret roof, 41.0 t, 0.47 m ground clearance, 580 mm track shoes, 4.27 m of track bearing on the ground. Those last two give a nominal ground pressure of 0.83 kg/cm2 against para. 51's 0.8 — the published figure agrees. At 41.0 t it sits inside Table 8's 25.1-42 t bracket, so KGUUB-2G would cover it, but the named spur assignment governs.

vehicles.class: Main battle tank (esasy söweş tanky) — T-90S, the export variant of the T-90; built under licence in India as the "Bhishma". Not a handbook entry
vehicles.manufacturer: Uralvagonzavod
vehicles.country: Russia
vehicles.notes: NOT A HANDBOOK VEHICLE. The handbook's Annex 14 catalogue stops at the Soviet-era types and never names a T-90 of any variant, so no securing method is assigned to this machine by name and none may be inferred from the tables that are. The figures here are the manufacturer's published specification for the T-90S export tank: hull 6.86 m (9.53 m overall with the gun trained forward), 3.78 m over the side skirts, 3.37 m over the tracks, 2.23 m to the turret roof, 46.5 t combat weight, 0.49 m ground clearance, 580 mm track shoes, and 4.27 m of track bearing on the ground (recorded as both the road-wheel base and, separately, as trackContactLengthCm, which is what the para. 51 ground-pressure limit is computed on: 46.5 t over 2 x 58 cm x 427 cm = 0.94 kg/cm2, against that paragraph's 0.8 kg/cm2 — the published nominal figure of 0.938 kg/cm2 agrees). The securing hardware listed is the handbook's own general provision for a tracked vehicle on an open wagon (wood stop blocks and wire lashings, para. 32), not a per-vehicle assignment. At 46.5 t the vehicle is above Table 8's 42 t KGUUB coverage, so approved method 1 does not apply to it, and above the 15 t special case for side-ramp loading in para. 51.

vehicles.class: Main battle tank (esasy söweş tanky) — T-80U, gas-turbine. Not a handbook entry
vehicles.manufacturer: Omsk Transmash
vehicles.country: Russia
vehicles.notes: NOT A HANDBOOK VEHICLE. The handbook's Annex 14 catalogue stops at the Soviet-era types and never names a T-80 of any variant, so no securing method is assigned to it by name and none may be inferred from the tables that are. The figures are the manufacturer's published specification for the T-80U: hull 7.0 m (9.65 m overall with the gun trained forward), 3.60 m over the side skirts, ~3.40 m over the tracks, 2.20 m to the turret roof, ~46 t combat weight, 0.45 m ground clearance, 580 mm track shoes, ~4.40 m of track on the ground. The 3D model is a parametric solid authored from the provided technical-orthographic reference, not a handbook plate. Securing hardware is the handbook's general provision for a tracked vehicle on an open wagon (wood stop blocks and wire lashings, para. 32), not a per-vehicle assignment.
